qualification: Pearson AAQ Applied Science Extended Certificate (first teaching 2025)
lessonAssumption: Approximately 50-60 minutes per slot; planning estimates, not official allocations. Revision sections follow taught content; this is not a new teaching course.

lessons.title: Types of Waves
lessons.scope: Transverse and longitudinal oscillations; energy transfer; compressions and rarefactions.

lessons.title: Wave Properties
lessons.scope: Amplitude, wavelength, frequency, periodic time, oscillation and wave speed; definitions and units.

lessons.title: Graphing Waves
lessons.scope: Read displacement-distance and displacement-time graphs; distinguish wavelength from period.

lessons.title: Wave Speed
lessons.scope: Use and rearrange v = fλ; use f = 1/T; convert wavelength and frequency units.

lessons.title: Phase Difference
lessons.scope: Signed displacement, coherence, phase and path difference; superposition; whole and odd half wavelengths.

lessons.title: Diffraction
lessons.scope: Apply interference ideas to the teacher-selected double-slit model; transfer ideas to grating contexts. Gratings forming line spectra link to Emission Spectra.

lessons.title: Emission Spectra
lessons.scope: Electron transitions and photons; gratings separate wavelengths; identify gases from line positions.

lessons.title: Standing Waves
lessons.scope: Incident/reflected-wave superposition, resonance, displacement nodes and antinodes. Adjacent displacement nodes are half a wavelength apart.

lessons.title: Harmonics
lessons.scope: Strings and open/closed pipes; harmonic patterns, pitch and v = √(T/μ); μ = mass/length.

lessons.title: Refraction
lessons.scope: Ray direction, normal, speed and refractive index; n = c/v and air-to-material sine ratios.

lessons.title: Critical Angle and TIR
lessons.scope: Both conditions for TIR; angle measured from normal; critical-angle calculations at glass-air boundaries.

lessons.title: Optical Fibres and Cladding
lessons.scope: Core/cladding boundaries, critical-angle comparison and repeated TIR; engineering, medicine and communication.

lessons.title: Inverse Square Law
lessons.scope: Relative intensity and I = k/r²; rearrangement, units and stated ideal-model assumptions.

lessons.title: Electromagnetic Spectrum
lessons.scope: Region ordering, overlapping ranges, frequency-wavelength relationship and equal vacuum speed.

lessons.title: Analogue and Digital Signals
lessons.scope: Continuous and discrete representations; binary waveforms and regeneration. Sampling depth remains an authored scope judgement.

lessons.title: Communication Applications
lessons.scope: Satellite links and GPS, mobile phones, Bluetooth, infrared and Wi-Fi; use evidence to justify choices.

lessons.title: Motion Quantities and Units
lessons.scope: SI symbols and units; speed conversions; scalar/vector distinctions; distance, displacement, speed and velocity.

lessons.title: Speed and Average Speed
lessons.scope: Distance/time calculations; total distance divided by total time; journeys with several stages.

lessons.title: Displacement-Time Graphs
lessons.scope: Interpret motion and calculate signed velocity from gradients.

lessons.title: Velocity-Time Graphs and Acceleration
lessons.scope: Interpret velocity-time traces; acceleration from gradient; a = (v-u)/t.

lessons.title: Distance and Displacement from Graphs
lessons.scope: Areas of rectangles/triangles; distinguish signed displacement from total distance when velocity changes sign.

lessons.group: Motion Equations: Velocity and Average Velocity
lessons.title: Motion Equations: Velocity and Average Velocity
lessons.scope: Constant acceleration; select and rearrange v = u + at and s = (u+v)t/2.

lessons.title: Motion Equations: Displacement
lessons.scope: Select and rearrange s = ut + ½at² and v² = u² + 2as; units and signs.

lessons.title: Measuring Acceleration and Accelerometers
lessons.scope: Trolley down a slope; measurements, graph evidence and uncertainty; fitness devices, phones and blood-pressure monitors.

lessons.group: Resultant Forces and Newton’s First Law
lessons.title: Resultant Forces and Newton’s First Law
lessons.scope: Force diagrams; balanced forces and constant velocity; a non-zero resultant changes velocity.

lessons.title: Mass, Weight and Inertia
lessons.scope: Distinguish mass and weight; inertia; gravitational field strength and W = mg.

lessons.title: Friction and Its Measurement
lessons.scope: F = μN; normal reaction; static threshold and constant-velocity kinetic-friction methods. N = mg only in the stated horizontal case.

lessons.title: Newton’s Second Law
lessons.scope: F = ma with resultant force; how mass and acceleration affect the required force.

lessons.title: Momentum
lessons.scope: p = mv; units, direction and comparisons of mass/speed.

lessons.title: Force and Change in Momentum
lessons.scope: F = (mv-mu)/t; stopping time, direction and average impact force.

lessons.title: Safety and Impact Protection
lessons.scope: Transport comparisons; air bags, seat belts, helmets, passenger cells and crumple zones; linked explanations.

lessons.title: Newton’s Third Law
lessons.scope: Interaction pairs act on different bodies; distinguish pairs from balanced forces on one body.

lessons.title: Drag and Terminal Velocity
lessons.scope: Changing resistive forces and resultant force; road vehicles, parachutes and objects falling through liquids.

lessons.title: Circuit Symbols, Quantities and Units
lessons.scope: Symbols and meanings of current, potential difference, energy, power and resistance; A, V, J, W and Ω.

lessons.title: Connecting Circuits and Meters
lessons.scope: Cells, supplies, lamps, resistors, variable resistors and switches; ammeters in series and voltmeters in parallel.

lessons.title: Resistance and V = IR
lessons.scope: Ohmmeter use on isolated, unpowered components; calculate and rearrange V = IR.

lessons.title: Filament Lamps and Diodes
lessons.scope: Use lamps and diodes in circuit contexts; interpret supplied current/potential-difference evidence.

lessons.title: Thermistors and LDRs
lessons.scope: Temperature/light-dependent resistance; specify thermistor behaviour in the question; use in sensor circuits.

lessons.title: Photodiodes and LEDs
lessons.scope: Distinguish detecting light from emitting light; use component behaviour in simple circuits.

lessons.title: Electrical Power
lessons.scope: P = IV and P = E/t; equation selection, rearrangement and units.

lessons.title: Electrical Energy
lessons.scope: E = VIt; calculate energy transferred and convert time units.

lessons.title: Domestic Energy Use
lessons.scope: Compare appliances; energy in kWh = power in kW × time in h. Cost calculations need supplied tariffs.

lessons.title: Fuses and Operating Current
lessons.scope: Use current/power evidence and supplied fuse ratings to select and justify a suitable fuse.

lessons.title: Energy Units and Temperature Scales
lessons.scope: J, kJ and MJ; Celsius/Kelvin conversion; temperature changes in K and °C have equal numerical size.

lessons.group: Temperature Change and Change of State
lessons.title: Temperature Change and Change of State
lessons.scope: Distinguish heating within a phase from melting/boiling; interpret heating/cooling evidence.

lessons.title: Specific Heat Capacity Calculations
lessons.scope: ΔQ = mcΔT; rearrangements and J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

lessons.title: Measuring Specific Heat Capacity
lessons.scope: Solids and liquids; electrical heating, measurements, energy losses and evaluation.

lessons.title: Specific Latent Heat Calculations
lessons.scope: ΔQ = mL; fusion and vaporisation; mass changes and J kg⁻¹.

lessons.title: Measuring Specific Latent Heat
lessons.scope: Fusion and vaporisation methods; measurements, energy losses and evaluation.

scopeNotes: The 12 teacher-supplied Waves headings are retained as groups. TIR has three lesson choices and Uses of Waves has three.

Waves: 16 selectable lesson sections, approximately 18 lesson slots. Forces: 17 sections, approximately 19 slots. Electricity: 16 sections, approximately 18 slots. Allow additional review and assessment time.

Diffraction is the existing teacher heading. Core practice uses double-slit superposition/path difference as requested. A1.3 grating contexts and A1.3.2 line spectra remain recorded; do not add a compulsory white-light rainbow task.
No grating-spacing or double-slit fringe-spacing equation is required by this pilot.
Forces and Electricity are mapped for expansion; their future sections must not start empty sessions.
General series/parallel resistor laws, projectile motion and impulse-area calculations are not added as separate required topics without further scope evidence.
